question.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=4{x}^{6} & \,⟹\,v=\int 4{x}^{6}\,dx=\frac{4{x}^{7}}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}4{x}^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{4{x}^{7}}{7}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}(\frac{4{x}^{7}}{7})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\frac{4({e}^{2})^{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})}{7}-\frac{4(1)^{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)}{7}]-\frac{4}{7}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}{x}^{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{14}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})}{7}-\frac{4{x}^{7}}{49}{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{8{e}^{14}}{7}-(\frac{4{e}^{14}}{49}-\frac{4}{49}) \\  & =\frac{1}{49}(56{e}^{14}-4{e}^{14}+4) \\  & =\frac{4}{49}(13{e}^{14}+1).\end{aligned}
$$
